description:
LANDED 0889c0b3a on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. Cold review with
prototype (approve-with-fixes, F1-F7 folded) + adversarial refutation.

THE CHANGE: the interpreter's RuntimeValueReader gains list_tail; the list
element question (matches_list_elements, was matches_list_head) reads the head
under PositionScope::Lowered exactly as the three lowerings do and, under Full,
walks EVERY element requiring some ONE clause's element question to admit them
all (each element asked under Full, so nested lists and lists in tuple positions
walk too); one cons-cell reading (list_shape_of) serves the axis and the walk;
the walk is capped at ELEMENT_WALK_LIMIT = 2^16 with a loud report and a unit
gate over a cyclic fake spine; surface_membership::escaped asks the value's own
axes (Lowered and not Full) and returns the witness -- the report prints the
rendered spine and the element that broke the most tolerant clause. Cost:
O(clauses x length), nested O(clauses x outer x inner), only under
FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP. Interp-only, for a stated reason: the
escaping POPULATION is door-independent by construction (all doors answer the
same Lowered question over the same plans); only the harm differs.

WHAT IT FOUND ON ITS FIRST PASS (597 fixtures, interp): base 0 everywhere (the
'inert by construction' claim, confirmed); head: 00277_enum_tier0_fixture 12
escapes at the settled arrival and under every arms: setting -- [1, :tail],
[3, 1, :tail], [5, 3, 1, :tail] (4 each) running the [integer] body because
construction wrapper w2's member SELECTION seats list(int) ahead of
list(int | :tail); 0 under wrappers:1 / wrappers:6 / wrappers:reverse (the
settled wrapper order is the only escaping order, fz-kdt.147's shape on the
list axis). Root cause: dispatch_from_callable_flow_edges never calls
routable_alternatives, so neither fz-kdt.143's drop nor fz-kdt.129/131's seat
runs on member selection -> fz-kdt.179 (cure) and fz-kdt.178 (the static census
never walks entry_dispatch or wrapper.selection). enum_predicate_search reads 1
under arms:6 only ([1, :ok] into a [integer] body): fz-kdt.131 facet 3 reached
by a real value for the first time. dispatch_list_head_separates reads 0 at
every setting -- its header's claim that [true, 1, :ok] runs the bool-list
body was FALSE: List.reduce_while_cont([head | tail], acc, r) hands the TAIL
to the recursive dispatch, so [false] and [] are what reach the [:false|:true]
arm; the pair is statically real and dynamically unreached (header corrected).
fz-kdt.146's blindness quantified by the review: 104 of 34,177 list projections
(0.30%) degrade to shape_only, 3 fixtures, all negated clauses.

GATES: SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS is a named per-fixture, per-arrival ratchet of
14 rows driven in process (settled 12 on 00277 attributed to 179; arms:6 12 +
enum_predicate_search 1 attributed to 131; three wrapper settings 0; the seven
tuple-era fixtures kept at 0); red at base (00277 0 vs 12). 15 fake-reader unit
gates drive the PRODUCTION matcher + observe; 5 go red with Full stubbed to
Lowered. Canon movers base vs head 0; behaviour movers interp/run 0; corpus
sweep knob on vs off ~10s vs ~11-13s. Every 'inert / until fz-kdt.144 / reads
zero / pinned at zero' sentence removed; dispatch-matrix.md's tripwire section
rewritten with the mechanism, cost, recipe, interp-only rationale and the
measured table.

COORDINATOR GATE (fresh, marker COORD-GATE-1788410942, HEAD 0889c0b3a): fmt clean; build 0 warnings; clippy -D warnings clean; lib 1612 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored; fixture_matrix --test-threads=1 485 / 0 / 9 (known-red set unchanged). Refuter: FIX-THEN-MERGE, folded (walk-limit boundary pinned, callable axis gated both ways, six more fake-reader cases, two doc over-claims restated, census row for dispatch_list_head_separates).

comments.text:
NOW LOAD-BEARING, not just an enhancement (fz-kdt.138, ce6768af4).

fz-kdt.138 retired the Scope-A carve-out, so every tuple position -- the
list-bearing ones included -- is decided by all three lowerings. Those
positions were the ENTIRE gap between PositionScope::Lowered and
PositionScope::Full, so the two readings are now the same function and
`surface_membership::escaped()` is literally `X && !X`.

CONSEQUENCE: fz-kdt.135's tripwire still reads 0 corpus-wide, but it reads 0
BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by measurement. It cannot fire on anything until
this ticket gives `Full` content the lowerings do not have -- the list TAIL.
The head is exact on rejection and erasing on acceptance, so a full re-ask
that walked the tail would find residue no emitted test can see (fz-kdt.131
facet 3's two pairs, plus analysis-excluded heterogeneous traffic).

The PositionScope plumbing was KEPT rather than deleted, precisely so this
ticket has its seat; runtime_type_predicate.rs's PositionScope doc and
.agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md's "The dynamic tripwire" both now say the
instrument is inert until this lands. That is the honest present-tense fact,
and it is also the argument for doing this one sooner rather than later: the
dispatch class currently has NO live dynamic instrument.

ABSORBS fz-kdt.135 (2026-09-02): the corpus-sweep integration and the triage of the surface-membership tripwire's findings are re-based on the list-TAIL reading, which is exactly what this ticket re-arms once heads carry predicates. The tuple reading has no gap left (119/138), so 135's original ten findings are closed; whatever the tail re-ask surfaces is triaged here.

Baseline note from fz-kdt.143's landing (d2a5f3510). The list-TAIL re-ask this ticket arms will find a SMALLER population than the pre-143 tree carried: every arm whose tail no test reads and whose stand-in the seat would never let it pass is gone from every callsite (corpus arm lines 126 -> 106 on 4 fixtures), so the tail-blind traffic left is exactly fz-kdt.131's facet 3 -- five pairs under the widest legal arrival, three at the settled one (enumerated on 131 today). dispatch_list_head_separates still carries a written-down reproducer, but its callsite now offers two arms ([:false | :true] and [int | :ok | :true]) rather than four; the [int] and [int | :ok] specializations remain in the artifact, reached by direct call edges from the callable-flow path. The tripwire will see [1, :ok] arriving at the [int | :ok | :true] body through the surviving arm, not at a [int] body through a dropped one.

title: The surface-membership tripwire walks the list spine: the dispatch class has its live dynamic instrument back, and its first pass found a blind routing in wrapper member selection
